Get trip segments' duration

Source: R/get_trip_segment_duration.R
get_trip_segment_duration.Rd

Returns the duration of segments between stops of each specified trip_id.

Usage

get_trip_segment_duration(
  gtfs,
  trip_id = NULL,
  unit = "min",
  sort_sequence,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL
)

Arguments

gtfs

A GTFS object, as created by read_gtfs().

trip_id

A string vector including the trip_ids to have their segments' duration calculated. If NULL (the default) the function calculates the segments' duration of every trip_id in the GTFS.

unit

A string representing the time unit in which the duration is desired. One of "s" (seconds), "min" (minutes, the default), "h" (hours) or "d" (days).

sort_sequence

Deprecated; do not supply. Timetables are now always sorted by stop_sequence. Passing TRUE raises a warning, and passing FALSE raises an error.

from

A string, in the "HH:MM:SS" format. Only segments that depart from their first stop at or after from are included. If NULL (the default), there is no lower limit.

to

A string, in the "HH:MM:SS" format. Only segments that depart from their first stop at or before to are included. If NULL (the default), there is no upper limit.

Value

A data.table containing the segments' duration of each specified trip.

Details

A trip segment is defined as the path between two subsequent stops in the same trip. The duration of a segment is defined as the time difference between its arrival time and its departure time, as specified in the stop_times file.

Existing _secs columns in stop_times (e.g. created with convert_time_to_seconds()) are used as-is, not recalculated from the time strings.

from and to are compared with the departure time of the first stop of each segment, read as the durations are (from departure_time_secs, if present), so use times past "24:00:00" for departures after midnight. For trips listed in frequencies, these are template times, not the times of each departure. Segments whose departure is blank are never included when from or to is given.

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo_gtfs.zip", package = "gtfstools")

gtfs <- read_gtfs(data_path)

trip_segment_dur <- get_trip_segment_duration(gtfs)
head(trip_segment_dur)
#>      trip_id segment duration
#>       <char>   <int>    <num>
#> 1: 2002-10-0       1 2.166667
#> 2: 2002-10-0       2 2.166667
#> 3: 2002-10-0       3 2.166667
#> 4: 2002-10-0       4 2.166667
#> 5: 2002-10-0       5 2.166667
#> 6: 2002-10-0       6 2.166667

# use the trip_id argument to control which trips are analyzed
trip_segment_dur <- get_trip_segment_duration(gtfs, trip_id = "CPTM L07-0")
trip_segment_dur
#>        trip_id segment duration
#>         <char>   <int>    <num>
#>  1: CPTM L07-0       1        8
#>  2: CPTM L07-0       2        8
#>  3: CPTM L07-0       3        8
#>  4: CPTM L07-0       4        8
#>  5: CPTM L07-0       5        8
#>  6: CPTM L07-0       6        8
#>  7: CPTM L07-0       7        8
#>  8: CPTM L07-0       8        8
#>  9: CPTM L07-0       9        8
#> 10: CPTM L07-0      10        8
#> 11: CPTM L07-0      11        8
#> 12: CPTM L07-0      12        8
#> 13: CPTM L07-0      13        8
#> 14: CPTM L07-0      14        8
#> 15: CPTM L07-0      15        8
#> 16: CPTM L07-0      16        8
#> 17: CPTM L07-0      17        8

# use the unit argument to control in which unit the durations are calculated
trip_segment_dur <- get_trip_segment_duration(gtfs, "CPTM L07-0", unit = "s")
trip_segment_dur
#>        trip_id segment duration
#>         <char>   <int>    <int>
#>  1: CPTM L07-0       1      480
#>  2: CPTM L07-0       2      480
#>  3: CPTM L07-0       3      480
#>  4: CPTM L07-0       4      480
#>  5: CPTM L07-0       5      480
#>  6: CPTM L07-0       6      480
#>  7: CPTM L07-0       7      480
#>  8: CPTM L07-0       8      480
#>  9: CPTM L07-0       9      480
#> 10: CPTM L07-0      10      480
#> 11: CPTM L07-0      11      480
#> 12: CPTM L07-0      12      480
#> 13: CPTM L07-0      13      480
#> 14: CPTM L07-0      14      480
#> 15: CPTM L07-0      15      480
#> 16: CPTM L07-0      16      480
#> 17: CPTM L07-0      17      480

# use the from and to arguments to keep only the segments that depart
# within a time of day
trip_segment_dur <- get_trip_segment_duration(
  gtfs,
  from = "07:00:00",
  to = "09:00:00"
)
head(trip_segment_dur)
#>      trip_id segment duration
#>       <char>   <int>    <num>
#> 1: 2002-10-0       1 2.166667
#> 2: 2161-10-0       1 1.733333
#> 3: 4491-10-0       1 1.600000
#> 4: 4491-10-0       2 1.600000
#> 5: 4491-10-0       3 1.600000
#> 6: 4491-10-0       4 1.600000
